review_type: independent stage and runtime visual review
readiness_decision: Credible and usable visual prototype; the frozen stage does not yet meet a 9/10 source-grounded finish. The main remaining material gaps are the hard black cast-shadow silhouettes and the dense, weakly shaded vapor bank.

included: UI obstruction in the supplied screenshots
excluded: Car model form, windshield/front repair and model rendering defects
Metric reconstruction accuracy or uniquely measured 6DoF
Native XR rendering and headset performance
Temporal smoothness beyond what still captures establish
scope.method: Fresh visual inspection of all 17 frozen V3 captures and 11 actual source frames. Read-only source inspection for likely causes. No browser, CLI app automation, live camera/input changes, source edits, or consultation of other judge reports.

hash_evidence.note: All 25 manifest entries matched at review start. Parent was then notified that live source/model could be unfrozen; conclusions apply to preserved V3 screenshots and the initially verified manifest state, not any later live edits.

observed_improvements.evidence: The bright rectangular floor island from V2 is substantially reduced in landscape-wide-end and portrait-wide-end. Most of the apron now falls into black gently; distant image edges are much less distracting. A faint black/background boundary remains, so this is improved rather than mathematically invisible.

Landscape show and portrait-release show a thin continuous center stripe through the main curve instead of the earlier flecks/short disconnected boxes. Surface mottling also gives the deck more material variation.

Descent and landing have more distinct front and trailing masses, a small saddle/gap between clusters, and a correctly local touchdown burst. The car is substantially obscured at landing and visible in the 13s clearance capture.

The main ramp, actor release, descent and touchdown region remain well framed in landscape and portrait. Full-path end-wide includes both distant ramp and car. Arc-length brace rhythm still reads much better than V1.
The 9.5s jets remain thin noisy pale blue-white wisps, compatible with the thin blue source jets in frame_19. They avoid the earlier solid opaque cone look.

material_gaps.evidence: A sharp, nearly black projected ramp/truss silhouette remains behind the ramp, plus an isolated dark airborne-car shadow. PCFSoft configuration has not visually made the high ramp shadow read like the broad, filled stage lighting in source wide_17 and overhead-37. Overhead is particularly revealing: the dark C and triangular truss pattern look cut out of the floor.
material_gaps.fix: Reduce the strength and sharpness of distant ramp/car cast shadows while retaining short wheel/contact grounding. Possible implementations include a softer broad key/fill balance or restricting high-ramp shadow casting. Verify the result visually in overhead and ready; a filter enum change alone is insufficient.
material_gaps.source_caveat: Source and app use different camera/light arrangements, so exact shadow position is not required. The material issue is the conspicuous hard black silhouette, not pixel correspondence.

material_gaps.evidence: At descent the front cluster and rear cluster separate slightly, but both remain rounded and similarly bright. At landing and especially 13s clearance, the trailing bank merges into a large white wall with small-scale noise and little coarse depth/shading. Actual source frames_23 through _27 also retain a substantial cloud, but show dark blue/gray interior mass, irregular tall lobes, rising separated wisps and coarse transparent gaps. The app therefore needs a different density/shading structure, not wholesale cloud removal.
material_gaps.likely_cause: Many overlapping billboards share opacity 0.6; random lifetime and three origin clusters do not prevent their interiors from accumulating near opacity one. The local burst also remains dense over several seconds. Procedural per-sprite lighting is largely hidden by repeated overlap.
material_gaps.fix: Introduce coarse spatial/age-dependent density holes and asymmetric rising lobes, lower the contribution of older overlapping sprites, and create darker cool/red-shaded interiors instead of relying only on high-frequency edge noise. Preserve enough local opacity to obscure the car at landing and preserve visible car clearance at 13s.
material_gaps.source_caveat: Cloud shape is turbulent and cannot match each source frame exactly. Large lingering cloud volume is supported by the source and should not itself be treated as a defect.

secondary_gaps.evidence: The regular identical cool spot pools, bright rectangular lamp lenses and clean parallel red boundary rails still read as a simplified recreation. Source wide_17 and overhead-37 have stronger grazing/reflected light, less regular brightness, white apron/track markings, and red spill. The current version captures the main dark-stage language but not all its texture and light variation.
secondary_gaps.fix: If further polish is desired, vary a few bank intensities/aims modestly and add only the source-supported dim white apron markings and rough grazing reflections. Avoid raising global fill.

secondary_gaps.evidence: The full-path end views retain a very faint straight black/background boundary near the lower floor extent, visible because the background is slightly lighter than faded floor output. It is much less prominent than V2.
secondary_gaps.fix: Match faded floor output to background color or make the final fade converge to that exact color. This is a minor finishing issue, not the current main blocker.

do_not_regress: Do not restore opaque cyan pressure cones; thin noisy jets are closer to the source.
Do not erase the lingering cloud globally: the source supports large vapor masses after touchdown.
Preserve local touchdown occlusion and the visible car at 13 seconds.
Preserve portrait action framing and the complete full-path wide option. The tiny end-wide actor is a natural coverage tradeoff, not a clipping defect.
Do not judge the current car-model form as stage quality or give the stage numerical motion-accuracy credit.
uncertainties: Still images cannot verify cloud temporal coherence, popping, sorting artifacts or replay smoothness.

The overhead screenshot appears to view the reverse/exterior side of the upper ramp, so the absent center stripe in that view is not counted as a new paint bug. Show/portrait-release demonstrate the stripe on the driving face.

No supplied 10.0s app capture directly isolates the stronger pressure-column phase visible in source frame_20. Current 9.5s jets are plausible; the stronger phase merits a later targeted view if needed.
The parent reports clean shader compilation logs after reload. This review independently verifies the deck is visible in the screenshots, but did not inspect live logs or automate the app.
conclusion: V3 improves floor continuity, deck paint and some cloud grouping. Stage score rises to 8.2/10. The remaining shadow and vapor finish is clearly visible in the frozen evidence and prevents 9/10 approval.
